description: Track an organization's carbon footprint from boundary definition through emission factor application to the final report.

steps.description: Define the organizational and operational boundaries for greenhouse gas reporting (Scope 1, 2, 3).

inputs.name: organization-structure
inputs.desc: Description of the organization's entities, facilities, and operations

inputs.name: reporting-period
inputs.desc: The time period covered by the report

outputs.name: reporting-boundary
outputs.desc: Defined boundary including which entities and scopes are in scope

outputs.name: data-collection-plan
outputs.desc: Plan listing the data sources and responsible parties for each scope

process: Identify all entities, facilities, and operations the organization controls or has equity in.
Select the consolidation approach (operational control, financial control, or equity share).
Define which Scope 1, 2, and 3 categories apply based on the organization's activities.
List the data sources and assign collection responsibilities for each category.

steps.description: Collect activity data for all emission sources within the reporting boundary.

inputs.name: data-collection-plan
inputs.desc: Plan listing data sources and responsibilities

outputs.name: activity-data-set
outputs.desc: Collected activity data organized by scope and category (fuel, electricity, travel, supply chain)

outputs.name: data-gaps
outputs.desc: List of any data gaps or estimates used

process: Collect Scope 1 data: fuel consumption, refrigerant leaks, process emissions.
Collect Scope 2 data: purchased electricity, steam, heating, and cooling.
Collect Scope 3 data: business travel, employee commuting, purchased goods, waste, upstream transportation.
Document any data gaps and the estimation methods used to fill them.

steps.description: Apply emission factors to activity data to calculate greenhouse gas emissions.

inputs.name: activity-data-set
inputs.desc: Collected activity data by scope and category

outputs.name: emissions-by-scope
outputs.desc: Calculated emissions in CO2e for each scope and category

outputs.name: methodology-notes
outputs.desc: Documentation of emission factors and calculation methods used

process: Select the appropriate emission factor database (EPA, DEFRA, IEA, or custom factors).
Apply emission factors to each activity data point, converting to CO2 equivalent.
Sum emissions by scope (1, 2, 3) and by category within each scope.
Document the emission factors, global warming potentials, and any assumptions.

steps.description: Compare the calculated footprint against baseline year and reduction targets.

inputs.name: emissions-by-scope
inputs.desc: Calculated emissions by scope and category

outputs.name: trend-analysis
outputs.desc: Year-over-year comparison of emissions against baseline and targets

outputs.name: carbon-footprint-report
outputs.desc: The complete carbon footprint report with findings and recommendations

process: Compare current period emissions to the baseline year by scope and category.
Assess progress against any reduction targets (science-based or internal).
Identify the largest emission sources and the categories with the most change.
Compile the full report with methodology, results, trends, and recommended actions.

description: Produce an ESG report from framework selection through data collection to final disclosure.

steps.description: Identify the applicable ESG reporting frameworks and their requirements.

inputs.name: company-profile
inputs.desc: Description of the company including industry, size, and stakeholders

inputs.name: reporting-requirements
inputs.desc: Any regulatory or investor requirements for ESG disclosure

outputs.name: selected-frameworks
outputs.desc: The frameworks to report against (GRI, SASB, TCFD, CDP, or others) with rationale

outputs.name: disclosure-requirements
outputs.desc: List of specific metrics and disclosures required by each framework

process: Assess which frameworks are required by regulation, stock exchange listing, or investor request.
Evaluate voluntary frameworks that align with the company's industry and materiality.
Map the overlapping requirements across frameworks to reduce duplication.
Produce the list of specific metrics, indicators, and narrative disclosures needed.

steps.description: Collect data across environmental, social, and governance pillars for the ESG report.

outputs.name: esg-data-package
outputs.desc: Collected data organized by E, S, and G pillars with sources

outputs.name: data-quality-notes
outputs.desc: Notes on data quality, gaps, and estimation methods

process: Collect environmental data: emissions, energy, water, waste, biodiversity impacts.
Collect social data: workforce demographics, health and safety, community impact, supply chain labor.
Collect governance data: board composition, executive compensation, ethics, risk management.
Document data sources, quality issues, and any estimates or proxies used.

steps.description: Calculate the ESG metrics and indicators required by the selected frameworks.

outputs.name: esg-metrics
outputs.desc: Calculated metrics and indicators mapped to each framework requirement

outputs.name: performance-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of performance against targets and prior year

process: Calculate each metric per the framework's methodology (intensity ratios, percentages, absolute figures).
Compare each metric to the prior year and any stated targets.
Flag metrics where performance declined or targets were missed.
Map each calculated metric to the specific framework disclosure it satisfies.

steps.description: Write the narrative disclosures and compile the ESG report.

inputs.name: esg-metrics
inputs.desc: Calculated metrics mapped to framework requirements

inputs.name: performance-summary
inputs.desc: Performance summary against targets and prior year

outputs.name: esg-report-draft
outputs.desc: The draft ESG report with data tables and narrative disclosures

outputs.name: review-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of framework requirements with completion status

process: Write the narrative for each pillar: strategy, risks, opportunities, and management approach.
Insert the data tables and metrics into the appropriate disclosure sections.
Complete the framework index (GRI content index, SASB disclosure table, or TCFD recommendations map).
Produce the review checklist confirming every required disclosure is addressed.

steps.description: Route the ESG report for internal review and approval before publication.

outputs.name: esg-report-final
outputs.desc: The approved ESG report ready for publication

outputs.name: assurance-plan
outputs.desc: Plan for external assurance if applicable

process: Route the draft to subject matter owners (environment, HR, legal, finance) for fact-checking.
Incorporate corrections and resolve any open data quality issues.
Obtain sign-off from the executive sponsor and the board (if required).
Determine whether external assurance is needed and outline the assurance scope.

description: Conduct a facility energy audit from billing analysis through field survey to the final recommendations report.

steps.description: Collect and analyze utility billing data to establish the facility's energy baseline.

inputs.name: facility-info
inputs.desc: Description of the facility including type, size, and operating hours

inputs.name: utility-bills
inputs.desc: At least 12 months of utility billing data (electric, gas, water)

outputs.name: energy-baseline
outputs.desc: Baseline energy consumption by fuel type, with seasonal patterns and cost breakdown

outputs.name: billing-anomalies
outputs.desc: Any anomalies or irregularities found in the billing data

process: Organize billing data by month, fuel type, and rate component (demand, energy, fixed charges).
Calculate annual energy consumption (kWh, therms) and cost by fuel type.
Identify seasonal patterns and peak demand months.
Flag any anomalies such as unusual spikes or billing errors.

steps.description: Survey the facility to inventory energy-consuming systems and identify waste.

inputs.name: billing-anomalies
inputs.desc: Anomalies to investigate during the survey

outputs.name: equipment-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of major energy-consuming equipment (HVAC, lighting, motors, envelope)

outputs.name: waste-observations
outputs.desc: Observed energy waste (running during unoccupied hours, poor insulation, leaks)

process: Walk the facility and inventory major equipment: HVAC units, lighting, motors, and plug loads.
Record nameplate data, operating schedules, and observed conditions.
Check the building envelope (insulation, windows, air sealing) for deficiencies.
Note operational waste: lights on in unoccupied areas, equipment running unnecessarily, temperature setpoints.

steps.description: Identify energy conservation measures and calculate savings and payback.

outputs.name: ecm-list
outputs.desc: List of energy conservation measures with estimated savings, cost, and simple payback

outputs.name: prioritized-measures
outputs.desc: Measures ranked by payback period and implementation ease

process: For each waste observation, define the corrective measure (retrofit, controls upgrade, behavioral change).
Estimate the annual energy savings for each measure using engineering calculations or benchmarks.
Estimate the implementation cost for each measure.
Calculate the simple payback period and rank measures by attractiveness.

steps.description: Compile the energy audit findings into the final report.

inputs.name: ecm-list
inputs.desc: Energy conservation measures with savings and costs

outputs.name: energy-audit-report
outputs.desc: The complete energy audit report with baseline, findings, and recommendations

outputs.name: implementation-plan
outputs.desc: Suggested implementation sequence and timeline

process: Compile the executive summary with total savings potential and top recommendations.
Include the baseline analysis, facility description, and equipment inventory.
Present each measure with its savings, cost, payback, and implementation notes.
Outline the recommended implementation sequence starting with no-cost and low-cost measures.

description: Procure renewable energy from needs assessment through contract negotiation to implementation.

steps.description: Assess the organization's energy consumption and renewable energy goals.

inputs.name: energy-consumption-data
inputs.desc: Annual energy consumption by facility and fuel type

inputs.name: sustainability-goals
inputs.desc: The organization's renewable energy or carbon reduction targets

outputs.name: renewable-requirement
outputs.desc: The amount of renewable energy needed (MWh) and the timeline

outputs.name: site-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of onsite renewable potential (roof space, land, solar resource)

process: Total the organization's annual electricity consumption across all facilities.
Determine what percentage must come from renewables to meet the stated goal.
Assess each facility for onsite generation potential (solar, wind, geothermal).
Calculate the gap between onsite potential and total renewable requirement.

steps.description: Evaluate the procurement options for renewable energy.

outputs.name: option-comparison
outputs.desc: Comparison of options (onsite solar, offsite PPA, virtual PPA, RECs, community solar) with pros, cons, and financials

outputs.name: recommended-approach
outputs.desc: Recommended procurement approach with rationale

process: Model onsite generation: installed cost, net metering value, maintenance, and payback.
Model offsite PPA or virtual PPA: contract price, term length, and basis risk.
Model unbundled RECs: current market price, vintage, and additionality.
Compare all options on cost, additionality, risk, and alignment with goals.

steps.description: Negotiate and execute the renewable energy contract.

outputs.name: contract-terms
outputs.desc: Negotiated contract terms (price, duration, settlement, credit)

outputs.name: procurement-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the procurement decision and contract

process: Issue the RFP to qualified developers or REC suppliers.
Evaluate bids on price, project quality, counterparty credit, and contract terms.
Negotiate the key terms: price escalator, curtailment risk, settlement mechanism, and termination.
Execute the contract and document the procurement decision for the sustainability report.

description: Set up a waste management program from waste audit through implementation to ongoing tracking.

steps.description: Audit the current waste streams to establish a baseline.

inputs.name: facility-description
inputs.desc: Description of the facility, operations, and current waste handling

inputs.name: waste-hauler-data
inputs.desc: Current waste hauler invoices and tonnage reports

outputs.name: waste-baseline
outputs.desc: Baseline waste generation by stream (landfill, recycling, compost, hazardous) with volumes and costs

outputs.name: contamination-findings
outputs.desc: Contamination issues found (recyclables in trash, trash in recycling)

process: Collect waste hauler invoices, tonnage reports, and disposal records for the past 12 months.
Conduct a physical waste sort to characterize the composition of each stream.
Calculate the current diversion rate (recycling + compost as a percentage of total waste).
Identify contamination issues and misrouted materials.

steps.description: Set reduction targets and plan the waste management improvements.

outputs.name: reduction-targets
outputs.desc: Waste reduction and diversion rate targets with timeline

outputs.name: improvement-plan
outputs.desc: Plan for infrastructure, signage, training, and procurement changes

process: Set diversion rate targets (e.g., from 30% to 60% within 18 months) based on the audit results.
Identify the highest-volume misrouted materials and design infrastructure to capture them.
Plan signage, bin placement, and color coding for each waste stream.
Identify upstream reduction opportunities (purchasing changes, reusable alternatives).

steps.description: Implement the waste management improvements and train staff.

outputs.name: implementation-record
outputs.desc: Record of changes made (bins, signage, contracts, training)

outputs.name: training-materials
outputs.desc: Training materials for employees on proper sorting

process: Install or reconfigure bins, compactors, and collection points per the plan.
Update waste hauler contracts to add or modify streams (organics, e-waste, textiles).
Train employees on proper sorting with hands-on demonstrations.
Set up the monthly tracking process for tonnage and diversion rate.

steps.description: Track waste diversion rates monthly and produce the waste management report.

outputs.name: diversion-metrics
outputs.desc: Monthly diversion rate, tonnage by stream, and cost data

outputs.name: waste-management-report
outputs.desc: Quarterly waste management report with trends and recommendations

process: Collect monthly tonnage data from waste hauler reports for each stream.
Calculate the diversion rate and compare against the target.
Identify any backsliding or contamination trends and address them.
Compile the quarterly report with metrics, trends, and next improvement actions.

description: Analyze utility rates to identify cost optimization opportunities.

steps.description: Collect and parse the current utility tariff schedules.

inputs.name: utility-accounts
inputs.desc: List of utility accounts with account numbers and service addresses

inputs.name: current-bills
inputs.desc: Recent utility bills showing the current rate schedule

outputs.name: tariff-details
outputs.desc: Parsed tariff components (demand charges, energy charges, time-of-use periods, fixed fees)

outputs.name: rate-alternatives
outputs.desc: Alternative rate schedules available from the utility

process: Identify the current rate schedule for each account from the bill or utility portal.
Parse the tariff into its components: demand charges (per kW), energy charges (per kWh), fixed fees, and any time-of-use periods.
Obtain the utility's full tariff book and identify alternative rate schedules the account may qualify for.
Note any pending rate cases or tariff changes that could affect future costs.

steps.description: Model the cost impact of rate optimization strategies.

outputs.name: optimization-scenarios
outputs.desc: Modeled scenarios (rate class change, demand management, time-of-use shifting) with projected savings

outputs.name: rate-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete rate analysis report with findings and recommendations

process: Recompute each account's cost under every eligible rate schedule to find the lowest-cost option.
Model demand management strategies: peak shaving, load shifting to off-peak hours.
Model time-of-use optimization: shifting discretionary loads to lower-cost periods.
Produce the report with current cost, optimized cost, annual savings, and implementation steps.

description: Build a water conservation plan from usage audit through implementation to tracking.

steps.description: Audit current water usage by source and application.

inputs.name: facility-water-data
inputs.desc: Water billing data and facility description

inputs.name: water-systems
inputs.desc: Description of water-using systems (fixtures, irrigation, cooling, process)

outputs.name: water-baseline
outputs.desc: Baseline water consumption by end use (domestic, irrigation, cooling, process)

outputs.name: waste-points
outputs.desc: Identified points of water waste (leaks, overwatering, inefficient fixtures)

process: Collect 12 months of water billing data and calculate average monthly consumption.
Estimate the breakdown by end use: domestic (restrooms, kitchens), irrigation, cooling towers, process.
Inspect for leaks, running fixtures, and overwatering.
Compare consumption per square foot or per occupant to benchmarks.

steps.description: Identify water conservation measures and calculate savings.

inputs.name: water-baseline
inputs.desc: Baseline water consumption by end use

outputs.name: conservation-measures
outputs.desc: List of measures with estimated water savings (gallons), cost, and payback

outputs.name: water-conservation-plan
outputs.desc: The complete water conservation plan with targets and implementation schedule

process: For each waste point, define the corrective measure (low-flow fixtures, smart irrigation, leak repair, recycling).
Estimate the annual water savings in gallons and the associated cost savings.
Estimate the implementation cost and calculate the simple payback.
Compile the plan with targets, prioritized measures, and an implementation schedule.

description: Conduct a sustainability audit covering environmental, social, and governance performance.

steps.description: Define the audit scope, criteria, and methodology.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Description of the organization, its operations, and its sustainability commitments

inputs.name: audit-objectives
inputs.desc: What the audit should assess and what standards or criteria to use

outputs.name: audit-plan
outputs.desc: Audit plan including scope, criteria, schedule, and evidence requirements

outputs.name: criteria-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of criteria organized by environmental, social, and governance categories

process: Define the organizational scope (which sites, operations, and time period).
Select the audit criteria (internal policy, ISO 14001, GRI, industry standards).
Build the criteria checklist organized by E, S, and G categories.
Schedule the audit activities and identify the evidence needed for each criterion.

steps.description: Collect evidence and assess performance against the sustainability criteria.

inputs.name: audit-plan
inputs.desc: Audit plan with scope and schedule

outputs.name: assessment-findings
outputs.desc: Findings for each criterion (conforming, non-conforming, observation)

outputs.name: improvement-opportunities
outputs.desc: Identified opportunities for improvement

process: Collect documentary evidence: policies, reports, records, and data.
Conduct interviews with responsible personnel for each area.
Assess each criterion against the evidence and classify as conforming, non-conforming, or observation.
Identify improvement opportunities beyond the minimum requirements.

steps.description: Compile the sustainability audit findings into the final report.

outputs.name: sustainability-audit-report
outputs.desc: The complete audit report with findings, non-conformances, and recommendations

outputs.name: corrective-action-plan
outputs.desc: Plan for addressing non-conformances with owners and deadlines

process: Summarize the overall audit results: number of conformances, non-conformances, and observations.
Detail each non-conformance with the evidence, the criterion violated, and the recommended corrective action.
Present the improvement opportunities with their potential impact.
Produce the corrective action plan with owners, deadlines, and verification methods.

description: Respond to a grid outage from detection through restoration to post-event review.

steps.description: Detect and confirm a grid outage event.

inputs.name: alarm-data
inputs.desc: SCADA alarms, smart meter data, or customer outage reports

inputs.name: grid-topology
inputs.desc: Description of the grid topology and feeder map

outputs.name: outage-scope
outputs.desc: Confirmed outage scope: affected feeders, estimated customers, and probable cause

outputs.name: initial-assessment
outputs.desc: Initial damage assessment and estimated restoration time

process: Correlate SCADA alarms, smart meter last-gasp signals, and customer reports to confirm the outage.
Identify the affected feeders and substations using the grid topology.
Estimate the number of affected customers.
Assess the probable cause (weather, equipment failure, vehicle accident, vegetation) from available data.

steps.description: Dispatch repair crews and manage the restoration sequence.

outputs.name: dispatch-plan
outputs.desc: Crew assignments, equipment needs, and restoration sequence

outputs.name: restoration-timeline
outputs.desc: Estimated restoration timeline by area or feeder

process: Prioritize restoration: critical facilities (hospitals, water treatment, emergency services) first.
Assign repair crews based on proximity, skillset, and equipment availability.
Sequence the restoration to maximize customers restored per switching operation.
Communicate the restoration timeline to dispatch, customer service, and public information.

steps.description: Communicate outage status and estimated restoration time to customers.

outputs.name: customer-notifications
outputs.desc: Notifications sent to affected customers with ETR updates

outputs.name: communication-log
outputs.desc: Log of all customer communications during the event

process: Send initial notification to affected customers with the outage cause and estimated restoration time.
Update customers as crews report progress or the timeline changes.
Send restoration confirmation when power is restored to each area.
Log all communications for the post-event review.

steps.description: Conduct the post-outage review and produce the event report.

outputs.name: outage-event-report
outputs.desc: Complete event report with timeline, cause, response actions, and metrics (SAIDI, SAIFI)

outputs.name: improvement-actions
outputs.desc: Actions to prevent recurrence or improve response time

process: Reconstruct the event timeline from detection through full restoration.
Calculate reliability metrics: SAIDI (duration), SAIFI (frequency), and CAIDI (average duration).
Identify what worked well and what could be improved in detection, dispatch, restoration, and communication.
Document the corrective actions to prevent recurrence (vegetation management, equipment replacement, relay coordination).

description: Benchmark building energy performance against comparable buildings to identify underperformers.

steps.description: Collect building characteristics and energy consumption data for benchmarking.

inputs.name: building-portfolio
inputs.desc: List of buildings with type, size, location, and year built

inputs.name: energy-data
inputs.desc: 12 months of energy consumption data for each building

outputs.name: building-profiles
outputs.desc: Standardized building profiles with characteristics and annual energy use

outputs.name: data-completeness
outputs.desc: Assessment of data completeness and any gaps

process: Collect building characteristics: gross floor area, building type, climate zone, occupancy hours, and occupant count.
Collect 12 months of energy data (electricity and fuel) for each building.
Standardize the data into consistent units (kBtu, kWh/sqft).
Flag any buildings with incomplete data and note the gaps.

steps.description: Normalize energy use for weather and occupancy to enable fair comparison.

inputs.name: building-profiles
inputs.desc: Building profiles with characteristics and energy data

outputs.name: normalized-eui
outputs.desc: Weather-normalized energy use intensity (EUI) for each building in kBtu per sqft

outputs.name: normalization-notes
outputs.desc: Documentation of normalization methods and weather data sources

process: Obtain heating and cooling degree day data for each building's climate zone.
Apply weather normalization to separate weather-dependent from base energy use.
Calculate the energy use intensity (EUI) in kBtu per square foot per year.
Adjust for occupancy differences where data is available.

steps.description: Compare each building's EUI against benchmarks and produce the benchmarking report.

outputs.name: benchmark-rankings
outputs.desc: Buildings ranked by EUI performance relative to their benchmark (Energy Star, CBECS median)

outputs.name: benchmarking-report
outputs.desc: Complete benchmarking report with rankings, outliers, and recommended next steps

process: Compare each building's EUI to the appropriate benchmark: Energy Star score, CBECS median, or portfolio average.
Rank buildings from best to worst performing relative to their benchmark.
Identify the top underperformers as candidates for energy audits.
Compile the report with the rankings, the comparison methodology, and recommended next steps for underperformers.
